feed.subtitle: News, research, video and things to read on AI, data and human capability for higher education.
feed.rights: Wits AHEAD Research Group, Wits School of Education, University of the Witwatersrand

entry.title: AI governance becomes higher education's top technology priority for the first time, EDUCAUSE survey finds
entry.summary:
EDUCAUSE, di US and Canada higher education tech association, say dia 2027 Top 10 IT Issues survey, wey dem do with 882 tech leaders, put di question of where AI dey add real value for number one position for di first time, e pass cybersecurity. Dem also put how to design AI structures for responsible innovation and how to build strong data governance inside di top ten, from di biggest number of people wey ever answer di survey.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar six, AI wey people fit trust, good behaviour, fairness and policy, dis result show say AI governance don become di main tech question for higher education, both for Global North and Global South, one change wey Wits AHEAD own policy work dey answer direct.

EDUCAUSE 2027 Top 10 IT Issues (via Campus Technology) · Higher education technology association survey

entry.title: University of Pretoria vice-chancellor says graduates need AI fluency and power skills, not just a degree, to find work
entry.summary:
For one article wey e write for Daily Maverick, Vice-Chancellor of University of Pretoria, Professor Francis Petersen, talk say graduate unemployment for South Africa still dey continue alongside skills wey employers no fit find, because universities still dey prepare students for one first job only instead of plenty career change for dia whole life. E say employers now expect graduates wey fit use AI well well, together with communication, teamwork and critical thinking, and e call for internship, work-integrated learning and support for entrepreneurship across every course of study.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar four, graduate capability, employability and fair transitions, one South Africa vice-chancellor wey call AI skill one main employability skill, together with di power skills wey employers already dey ask for, dey strengthen di work wey Wits AHEAD dey do to connect analytics, curriculum and wetin happen to graduates.

Daily Maverick (Professor Francis Petersen, Vice-Chancellor, University of Pretoria) · University vice-chancellor opinion article, established press

entry.title: Bangladeshi university students show moderate knowledge but mixed practice on AI-assisted plagiarism, study finds
entry.summary:
One survey of 386 students for government and private universities for Bangladesh, wey dem publish inside AI and Ethics journal, see say students sabi small-small, but dia practice no dey consistent when e come to AI-giarism, wey mean to use generative AI tools make work wey dem go present as dia own, even though dia mind about academic honesty dey good well well. Dis attitude change well well according to di type of university, where dem dey live, publishing experience and course of study, and students wey get training for academic writing show better practice.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar one, generative AI for higher education, assessment and honesty, dis finding say good attitude no mean good practice dey remind us say na AI literacy, no be policy alone, go protect assessment honesty, one question wey still dey important well well for Wits AHEAD Global South partners.

AI and Ethics (Noakhali Science and Technology University) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Lisbon university combines early-warning alerts with compulsory AI literacy to protect first-year students, study finds
entry.summary:
One case study wey cover di whole Iscte, University Institute of Lisbon, wey dem publish inside Education Sciences journal, describe nine years of combining one rule-based early-warning system wey dey flag first-year students wey dey risk with one critical AI-literacy course wey be compulsory for one campus and optional for di oda one. Di authors report say academic risk dey concentrate for groups wey people fit identify, and say common AI-literacy baseline fit work, but support dey reach only small part of students wey dem flag, and predictive models wey dem train with one set of students no dey work well for di next set.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar two, predictive analytics for student success, retention and early warning, dis honest finding, say support and prediction both get real limit, na useful warning for Wits AHEAD as e dey weigh dia own early-warning tools against di resources wey dem need to act on am.

Education Sciences (Iscte - University Institute of Lisbon) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: OECD data show graduate unemployment rising for the first time since its records began
entry.summary:
OECD Education at a Glance 2026 report, wey dem launch on 29 September 2026, find out say unemployment among young people wey dey 25 to 34 years wey get university degree rise by 0.4 percentage points for member countries between 2023 and 2025, while unemployment among dose wey only get secondary education fall by 0.2 percentage points, e narrow di usual gap: na di first time dis kain reversal happen since di data series start for year 2000. South Korea show di pattern well well: 71.1% of im young people wey dey 25 to 34 get tertiary qualification, pass OECD average wey be 47.5%, but im graduate employment rate of 80.1% dey below OECD average of 86%.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 4, graduate capability, employability and just transition, na di clearest OECD-wide sign so far say degree advantage for job market dey shrink, just as AI dey change entry level work, one trend wey Wits AHEAD suppose follow well against dia own South Africa graduate destination data.

OECD, Education at a Glance 2026 (via UPI) · Intergovernmental body data, reported by an international wire service

entry.title: Côte d'Ivoire launches UNESCO-backed AI training for 3,000 vocational education teachers
entry.summary:
Ivory Coast Minister Delegate for Technical Education and Vocational Training, Jean-Louis Moulot, launch one programme on 25 September 2026 to train 3,000 teachers, pedagogical supervisors and administrators for technical and vocational education for how to use artificial intelligence, with UNESCO dey give technical support. Di first phase run from 1 October to 30 December 2026, dem go train 1,000 teachers for Abidjan on AI basics, how to use am for education, assessment methods, ethics and data security, before dem go check di pilot for make e expand go di whole country.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 3, AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, na rare programme wey government lead, UNESCO support, wey dey train di teacher-trainers demsef, no be only dia students, one model wey Wits AHEAD fit use for dia own work with South African technical and vocational colleges.

TrendsnAfrica · Government programme launch with UNESCO technical support, reported by regional press

entry.title: Ghana commits to train 100,000 TVET facilitators in AI under new UNESCO and Microsoft partnership
entry.summary:
Ghana Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Service sign agreement with UNESCO, KPMG and Microsoft on 30 September 2026, to train at least 100,000 TVET facilitators for artificial intelligence and digital skills, under di AI EmpowerED programme. TVET Service director general, Dr Eric Kofi Adzroe, talk say di partnership show one shift to system wey match industry, wey technology dey power, and wey dey focus on result, while UNESCO country representative, Edmond Moukala, sign di agreement for di organisation side.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 4, wey be graduate capability, employability and just transition, to give technical and vocational instructors AI skills for dis kain scale fit change how one whole generation of African artisan and technician go enter job market wey AI don change, na pattern wey Wits AHEAD dey watch to learn wetin fit work for South Africa own TVET sector.

Graphic Online · National press, government partnership announcement

entry.title: US learning platform data shows AI tools trail far behind other classroom technology
entry.summary:
Di new EdTech Top 40 report wey Instructure bring out, wey dem base on data wey no show who be who, from 19.5 million higher education users wey dey use dia Canvas learning platform between September 2025 to April 2026, show say Google Gemini, di AI tool wey people dey use pass, na only 87,788 users for 211 schools e reach, e no even enter di top 100 tools wey people dey use. Old tools like McGraw Hill, wey get 11.3 million users, Watermark course evaluations and Zoom, still dey waka pass am well well. Instructure vice president, Ryan Lufkin, talk say universities dey sign big AI deal for di whole school but dem never put di tools inside everyday class work.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, wey be generative AI for higher education, di gap wey dey between AI license wey school buy and how dem dey really use am for class, na warning wey Wits AHEAD dey watch: to buy AI tool access no be di same as to put am inside teaching and assessment, and dis one connect well well to di group work on how to really use AI.

Inside Higher Ed · Established press report on industry usage data

entry.title: UNESCO programme trains over 100 rural teachers and principals across China and Southeast Asia in AI and STEM
entry.summary:
UNESCO announce for 30 September 2026 say dia China-Southeast Asia Capacity Development Programme for Teachers and Principals, wey happen for Beijing from 17 to 23 August 2026 under di theme 'STEM and AI: Empowering Rural Teachers for Digital Transformation', bring together education policy people, school leaders, teachers and experts wey pass one hundred, from China and Southeast Asia countries. Dem organise am togeda with UNESCO International Research and Training Centre for Rural Education, SEAMEO RECSAM, di UNESCO Chair on Artificial Intelligence in Education for Beijing Normal University, and OECD, and di programme focus on how to use AI and STEM teaching to push digital equity for rural communities wey no get enough support. Professor Shahbaz Khan, director of UNESCO Regional Office for East Asia, call for AI wey 'centre on human, dey follow ethics, and carry everybody come' for education.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 3, wey be AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, how di programme insist say technology fit support but e no fit replace rural teachers, na pattern wey Wits AHEAD fit use for dia own work of preparing teacher trainers for places wey no get enough resource for di Global South.

UNESCO · Intergovernmental body

entry.title: Ethiopia's Education Ministry says AI will support, not replace, teachers as it expands digital learning
entry.summary:
Ethiopia Minister of Education, Berhanu Nega, talk for 29 September 2026 say teachers across di kontri dey get support to use artificial intelligence for lesson preparation, content development, student support and assessment, togeda with how dem dey make di ministry Education and Higher Education Management Information Systems digital. Di Minister talk say dem dey bring AI to make teachers capacity strong, no be to replace dem, as part of bigger push for online, blended and micro credential learning, and better digital connection for universities and schools. E call for education system to pass memorisation and raise critical thinkers wey fit 'work togeda with machines'.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, wey be generative AI for higher education, and pillar 5, wey be analytics and data for education systems, one national ministry wey dey openly commit say AI go support teachers instead of to replace dem, togeda with system level data reform, na di kain policy sign wey Wits AHEAD dey watch across di Global South.

allAfrica (Ethiopian News Agency) · National press, government ministry announcement

entry.title: Africa must build its own AI solutions rather than import them, says UN scientific panel member
entry.summary:
Girmaw Abebe Tadesse, wey dey lead Microsoft AI for Good Lab for Kenya and dey sidon for United Nations Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, tell UN News during UN High Level Week for New York on 25 September 2026 say African kontris suppose first sabi dia own problem before dem go adopt technology wey dem design for anoda place. E talk say stakeholders, including higher education institutions, governments, development partners and technology companies, suppose share knowledge togeda to build solution wey fit local reality, instead of to dey do di same work twice, and e point out say African young people don already dey innovate, dey use technology solve community wahala.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, wey be responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, one UN science adviser wey openly name universities as important partner for AI agenda wey local people dey lead, dey support wetin Wits AHEAD dey always talk about: say African research and solution matter pass borrowed framework.

allAfrica (UN News) · UN News Service, intergovernmental body

entry.title: Cape Town hosts first African THE World Academic Summit as Wits and four other South African universities rise in the world rankings
entry.summary:
The Times Higher Education (THE) World Academic Summit open for University of Cape Town on 30 September 2026, na first time dis event dey happen for Africa, and dem launch di THE World University Rankings 2027 for di same time. Now, five South African universities dey among di top 500 for di world, Wits inside am for position 301 to 325. University of Cape Town climb to joint 147th position, di best rank wey dem don get for seven years. Cape Town vice chancellor, Mosa Moshabela, talk say di university don switch off dia AI detection tools, so dem fit face teach students how to use AI di correct way, while di Minister of Higher Education, Buti Manamela, talk say six out of every ten young South Africans no get work.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1 wey be generative AI for higher education, di decision wey University of Cape Town take to drop AI detection and instead teach students how to use am well, na shift for assessment policy wey Wits AHEAD dey follow across di whole sector; di way di rankings dey rise, add to di unemployment number wey di Minister mention, show why AI, analytics and graduate skill matter for every South African university, Wits inside.

Daily Maverick · Established press

entry.title: Alliance for African Partnership meets in Dar es Salaam and puts AI skills at the centre of regional cooperation

category.term: Africa (Tanzania, hosted by the University of Dar es Salaam)

entry.summary:
The Alliance for African Partnership, na group of 12 universities from 10 African countries wey Michigan State University dey lead, hold dia 2026 annual meeting for University of Dar es Salaam from 16 to 22 September. Deputy Vice-Chancellor for Research, Nelson Boniface, tell delegates say universities must update dia curriculum and train lecturers so dat graduates no go dey left behind by artificial intelligence, e add say AI literacy don become skill wey every student need, no be only computer science students.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 4 wey be about graduate capability, employability and just transitions, di Alliance call for curriculum reform and lecturer training for ten African countries agree well well with wetin Wits AHEAD dey talk say every course, no be only STEM, need AI literacy make African graduates fit still get work.

allAfrica.com, from the Daily News (Tanzania) · Established African news service

entry.title: Morgan State University wins 10 million dollar federal grant to build a trusted AI research institute
entry.summary:
Morgan State University, na historically Black university wey dey Baltimore, don receive 10 million dollars federal money from United States government to build Institute for Trusted Autonomous Networks, wey dem dey call TITAN. Na US senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks announce dis one on 16 September 2026. Dis grant wey go last five years go fund research and PhD training for artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and quantum enhanced security, and e go help Morgan State reach the highest level among American research universities.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 3, wey be AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, di way TITAN dey focus on training PhD researchers for one historically Black university show how targeted AI research money fit widen who dey lead AI research, one question wey Wits AHEAD dey track for equity for STEM worldwide.

CBS News Baltimore · Established press

entry.title: MIT trains faculty from other universities to teach AI across disciplines
entry.summary:
MIT Schwarzman College of Computing test one week-long workshop wey dey train lecturers from oda universities make dem fit teach artificial intelligence and machine learning inside dia own subject, dem adapt am from MIT own course, 'Modelling with Machine Learning'. Di first workshop for July 2026 bring together 19 lecturers from seven institutions, including Allen University, Babson College, Brandeis University and University of Massachusetts Lowell, and pass six MIT instructors teach sessions for finance, computer science and sustainability.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 3, wey be AI and analytics for STEM and teacher training, dis pilot dey solve one problem wey Wits AHEAD sef dey face: lecturers wey no be computer science people need real hands-on training before dem fit teach AI literacy well well inside dia own subject.

MIT News · University announcement

entry.title: UNESCO survey finds most Latin American and Caribbean universities use AI, but few have a strategy
entry.summary:
UNESCO International Institute for Higher Education in Latin America and the Caribbean, wey be IESALC, join United Nations University Institute for the Advanced Study of Sustainability survey 200 higher education institutions for 19 countries, and dem release di result on 8 September 2026, during UNESCO Digital Learning Week. Di survey show say 87 percent of di institutions don already dey use AI for one area of dia work, mostly for teaching, but na only 26 percent get official AI strategy. Most of di AI moves dey start from lecturers, researchers or students, no be from institution leaders.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, wey be responsible AI, ethics, fairness and policy, dis gap wey dey between almost everybody dey use AI and official governance wey still rare for Latin America and Caribbean, be di same pattern Wits AHEAD dey track across di whole Global South, where everyday practice dey run ahead of institution policy.

UNESCO IESALC and United Nations University · Intergovernmental higher education body report

entry.title: University of Colorado system adopts a living policy for responsible use of AI
entry.summary:
Di new Administrative Policy Statement 6012 for University of Colorado system, wey dem call Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence, start to dey work from 24 August 2026, and dem talk about am for di university policy blog on 21 September. E set expectation for di whole system about academic honesty, data protection, transparency and how to check say AI-generated work correct. Dem show clearly say dis policy suppose change as students and staff dey give feedback.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, wey be generative AI for higher education, teaching, assessment and honesty, one big public university system wey choose to treat dia AI rules as tin wey go still dey change, no be fixed policy, dey give Wits AHEAD one Global North comparison for di kain governance choice wey e dey track for Global South.

University of Colorado · University policy announcement

entry.title: University of Pretoria trains future teachers in "prompt literacy" for the AI classroom
entry.summary:
Researchers for University of Pretoria Department of Early Childhood Education, wey Dr Joyce West and Dr Kayla Willemse dey lead, dey run one multi-phase study on prompt literacy, wey be di ability to give generative AI clear instruction while still dey check wetin e produce with critical eye. Di project dey train future teachers to use AI as classroom tool wey dem fit work with, no be tin to fear, through activities like to create children story and digital material, while dem dey watch for bias, mistake and copyright wahala for wetin AI produce.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 3, wey be AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis study dey face one gap wey Wits AHEAD dey watch well well: whether dem dey really teach new teachers to question wetin AI produce, no be just how to produce am.

Future SA, reporting University of Pretoria research · South African higher education press, reporting university research

entry.title: East African universities and Arizona State University partner to build "AI-ready" higher education
entry.summary:
Inter-University Council for East Africa, wey be di higher education body for East African Community, announce partnership on 9 September 2026 with Arizona State University University Design Institute to help East African universities prepare well for AI. Di work cover four areas: leadership and governance, staff training, research setup, and learning between institutions. Di Design Institute bring experience from 26 countries and pass 140 institutions, seven of dem for Africa.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 5, wey be analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, dis partnership show say regional higher education body fit build AI capacity for plenty universities same time, one model wey Wits AHEAD fit compare with im own reach for Southern Africa.

Inter-University Council for East Africa · Intergovernmental higher education body announcement

entry.title: Maharashtra sets up a state committee to govern AI and data dashboards across its universities
entry.summary:
Di Higher and Technical Education Department for Maharashtra state for India don release government resolution wey set up AI, Data Analytics and Dashboard Governance Committee, wey Professor Rajnish Kamat, wey be vice-chancellor of Shivaji University for Kolhapur, dey head. For di three years wey di committee go last, di nine members must set state AI strategy, choose wetin dem go prioritize for generative AI, machine learning and natural language processing, make di data wey dey for existing student, exam and scholarship dashboards match well, and build automatic trend analysis and risk forecasting inside portal wey just dey report numbers now, while dem still follow cybersecurity and privacy rules. Di committee go report every three months to di department top officials.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 5, wey be analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, na one of di first state governments anywhere wey put standing committee wey get accountability in charge to turn simple reporting dashboard to real early-warning and decision-support system, one model wey Wits AHEAD fit point to when dem dey argue for di same change for South Africa.

Government of Maharashtra, Higher and Technical Education Department · State government resolution, reported by regional press

entry.title: Telkom Foundation, BCX and Alibaba Cloud partner with Wits to give students AI-powered coding tools
entry.summary:
Telkom Foundation, BCX and Alibaba Cloud don team up with University of Witwatersrand (Wits) to give around 165 third-year Computer Science students access to Qoder, na Alibaba AI-powered software platform, for dia academic software projects. Di Qoder Programme wan give students real hand-on experience with AI-assisted coding tools before dem enter workplace wey dis kind tools don become normal. E also wan strengthen di link between Wits curriculum and how industry dey work for real. Professor Richard Klein, wey be head of Wits School of Computer Science and Applied Mathematics, talk say di curriculum need to change as dis kain global changes dey happen.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 4, wey be graduate capability, employability and just transitions, na real step wey Wits demsef take to close di gap between wetin Computer Science graduates dey learn and di software engineering jobs wey AI don already boost, wey dem go enter, for one scale wey Wits AHEAD fit track and build on.

Wits University · University announcement

entry.title: Systematic review of 124 studies finds AI's value in education depends on governance, not the technology, and flags a Global South research gap

category.term: Global (evidence base: Central Asia, East Africa)

entry.summary:
One systematic review wey researchers from universities for Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tanzania do, put together 124 studies wey dem publish between January 2020 and January 2026, about how AI dey change education. Di review find real but no-balance shift, from dem just dey use AI tools one by one, go more adaptive teaching wey dey based on data, and e conclude say whether dis change go help or spoil students dey depend on governance and institution kain environment, no be di technology itself; human judgement and teacher role must remain central, instead make dem treat AI as im get power for imsef. Di people wey write di study also find say di studies wey dem review dey mostly for English language, while Global South, indigenous and multi-language views still dey largely missing.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, wey be responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, na peer-reviewed confirmation, wey researchers wey dey base for Central Asia and East Africa demsef do, of di exact evidence gap wey dey push Wits AHEAD own work: di literature wey suppose guide AI policy for education no dey really include di Global South voices wey e suppose listen to.

Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Business schools bring back oral defences as AI use rises
entry.summary:
Some top business school for Europe, like Insead, Imperial College Business School and HEC Paris, dey bring back oral defence, paper-and-pen exam and close supervision assessment, because generative AI don make di normal take-home case study no fit trusted again. Peter Todd, wey dey Imperial, talk say staff no fit sure again wetin written work dey show unless student defend am for mouth or write am under supervision; HEC Paris don start to dey alternate between assessment wey no get computer and di one wey get computer. Di Graduate Management Admission Council talk say assessment standard need to clear well well if business qualification wan keep dia value.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, wey be generative AI for higher education: teaching, assessment, integrity, as top business school dey comot take-home work completely, instead of just patch am small, e show wetin Wits AHEAD need think about assessment integrity for African universities wey dey face di same pressure, but wey no get as e be resources to run oral or supervised exam.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: African curriculum experts meet in Dar es Salaam to confront the AI challenge in teacher education
entry.summary:
Di sixth conference of African Curriculum Association happen for Dar es Salaam from 22 to 25 September 2026, e bring together curriculum developer, teacher trainer, researcher and policymaker from all over di continent. Tanzania Institute of Education director general, Dr Aneth Komba, and ACA secretary general, Dr Gertrude Namubiru, lead di talk about how African curriculum and teacher training suppose adapt to artificial intelligence and fast tech change, while e still dey based for local skills and community need. Di conference wan produce one Dar es Salaam Declaration on Education Transformation in Africa, wey follow African Union Agenda 2063 and di fourth Sustainable Development Goal.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 3, wey be AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, one continent-wide meeting wey talk about how teacher training itself must change for classroom wey AI don shape connect well well with Wits AHEAD work on wetin dem wey dey train teachers need to know, no be only wetin dem go teach students.

The Citizen (Tanzania) · Established national press

entry.title: Universities must teach people to work ‘with AI, not for AI’, says King's College London head
entry.summary:
For di 2026 Korea Times Global Conference wey happen for Seoul, King's College London Vice-Chancellor, Shitij Kapur, talk say universities must make sure say people dey work with artificial intelligence, no be say dem dey work for am. E lay out five wahala wey universities suppose carry: to rethink wetin learning mean, to prepare graduates for job market wey dey change, to protect careful research, to make AI work for everybody good, and to make sure say e strengthen human power instead of replace am. Kapur talk say di way AI go develop no dey fixed, and say universities and countries fit still shape how e dey built and how e dey used, instead of just accept wetin tech industry give dem.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, wey be responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, as one big vice-chancellor put universities for centre of how AI go shape, instead of just to dey react, e support wetin Wits AHEAD dey stand for: higher education for Global South suppose help set di rules for how AI go enter, no be just to dey collect tools wey dem build for another place.

University World News · Established higher education press

entry.title: Latin America's universities embrace AI faster than they can govern it, new study finds
entry.summary:
One UNESCO-IESALC study wey cover 200 higher education institution for 19 country for Latin America and Caribbean find out say 87 percent of dem don already dey use artificial intelligence for some part of dia work, but na only 26 percent get any formal AI framework. Private non-profit university dey adopt am pass, na 84 percent, public own na 68 percent, private-for-profit own na 52 percent, and 55 percent of all di institutions no get budget wey dem set aside for AI. Borhene Chakroun of UNESCO talk say to fully enjoy di benefit, dem need to keep dey invest for access and capacity, with governance wey go make sure say di use dey ethical, transparent and accountable.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, wey be responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, dis study show exactly di kind risk wey Wits AHEAD dey warn about: public universities, wey dey serve students wey no get plenty option, dey adopt AI fast fast for classroom, but dem dey lag behind well well for governance, training and money to use am well.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press, reporting a UNESCO IESALC study

entry.title: African universities can drive talent development at scale, Mastercard Foundation tells Accra convening
entry.summary:
For di first Higher Education Transformation Convening wey happen for Accra on 22 September 2026, Dr John Nkengasong of Mastercard Foundation describe African universities as 'engines of prosperity' and human capital infrastructure wey must join their teaching with wetin labour market and industry need. Di event give five institutions di Africa Higher Education for Transformation (AHEFT) Prize: Addis Ababa University, 2iE, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Muni University and University of Rwanda. Di foundation talk again say dem wan help 30 million young Africans, 70 percent of dem women, find dignified work by 2030.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 4, wey be graduate capability, employability and just transitions, as one big funder dey see universities as talent infrastructure, and still count AI among di forces wey dey change work, e make Wits AHEAD work strong on which graduate skills really dey carry people reach dignified work for African job markets.

University World News · Established higher education press

entry.title: 'Syncopathy' and AI: African HE must choose verification
entry.summary:
For one article for University World News, Dr Kende Kefale of University of Cape Town bring out new word 'syncopathy' for AI output, like citations and arguments, wey look correct but nobody check am, and e talk say universities get di same problem because to check work cost plenty and nobody dey see am, but to produce work cheap and easy to count. E suggest say institutions suppose show how much work human being don check before dem give certificate, say every automatic detection system must get one named person wey go answer for im mistakes, and say di record of checking suppose be permanent output of di institution. E point to South Africa draft National AI Policy wey government withdraw for April 2026 after dem find fake citations for im reference list.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, wey be AI wey people fit trust, good behaviour, fairness and policy, dis argument give Wits AHEAD one practical way to think about AI governance for African universities, wey put di cost of checking and di responsibility for machine judgement on top institutions, no be on students.

University World News · Commentary by a University of Cape Town academic in established higher education press

entry.title: From AI use to funding cuts: how provosts are navigating 2026
entry.summary:
Inside Higher Ed 2026 survey of 376 chief academic officers (provosts), wey Hanover Research run, show say about seven out of ten dey use AI for their own work at least once every week, but only one out of ten talk say their institution get central AI strategy. Only 12 percent see better department workflow from di institution AI investment and 8 percent see change for di whole institution, while 15 percent never invest at all. Staff skills and capacity (51 percent) and resistance from lecturers and staff (50 percent) na di main wahala wey dem mention.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 5, wey be analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, di gap between how leaders dey use AI by themselves and wetin di institution plan na exactly where Wits AHEAD dey push for evidence-based, system-level decisions about AI for universities.

Inside Higher Ed · Established higher education press; national survey fielded by Hanover Research

entry.title: Record number of graduates pushes youth unemployment to 18.9%
entry.summary:
Unemployment for young people wey dey city for China, from 16 to 24 years and no be students, rise from 17.9 percent for July reach 18.9 percent for August 2026, according to National Bureau of Statistics figures wey University World News report. Dis rise follow record 12.7 million university graduates dis summer, and na di highest since dem change di way dem dey count am for 2023. Di report point to weak demand inside di country and how AI dey spread as di things wey dey press down hiring for entry-level jobs.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 4, wey be graduate capability, employability and just transitions, wetin dey happen for China show say to expand higher education alone no fit guarantee job when AI dey change entry-level work, and Wits AHEAD go compare dis lesson with graduate job markets for South Africa and di Global South.

University World News (from the South China Morning Post) · Established higher education press reporting national statistics

entry.title: Ten-country African university alliance pushes joint research and AI skills
entry.summary:
Di Alliance for Africa Partnership, wey be group of 12 institutions from 10 African kontris wey Michigan State University dey anchor, use im annual meeting for Dar es Salaam on 22 September 2026 to call for joint research wey tight well well and make universities build AI skills enter dia curriculum. Professor Nelson Boniface of University of Dar es Salaam tell di delegates say to sabi AI don be basic requirement for every graduate, no be only for those wey dey code, im push say make universities, industry and government link up well to turn research to real solution.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 4 na about AI, wetin graduates fit do, work opportunity and just transition. African university alliance wey get kontris ten wey put AI skills and joint research for dia own agenda, without wait for outside framework, na real example of di cross-border collaboration wey Wits AHEAD dey study, and e dey remind us say di continent dey solve im skills gap from inside.

Tanzania Daily News, via allAfrica · African press wire service

entry.title: Report warns AI adoption in US colleges is outpacing student safeguards
entry.summary:
New report from Student Defense SHAPE initiative, wey Inside Higher Ed cover on 18 September 2026, find out say United States colleges don mix AI enter admissions, financial aid, advising and teaching faster pass how dem build protection for students. E identify algorithm bias for aid decisions, data privacy gap, and loss of real learning community as di main wahala, e dey call on institutions make dem set clear governance and transparency rules before dem deploy AI systems more.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, wey be AI wey people fit trust, good behaviour, fairness and policy, dis report na real checklist of where AI governance for higher education dey lag behind wetin dey happen for ground, e go helep test Wits AHEAD im own guide on transparency and accountability against system wey don go far well well for AI adoption.

Inside Higher Ed · Established higher education press

entry.title: UNESCO: over 25 education ministers declare AI must serve the 'common good'
entry.summary:
More pass 25 education ministers and senior officials wey meet for UNESCO Digital Learning Week for Paris agree one joint statement on 8 September 2026 say education must remain human right and common good as AI dey spread enter classroom and universities. Di statement give eight priorities, wey include make AI systems dey auditable and under public oversight, and make dem protect teachers' voice on classroom technology. E quote one UNESCO survey wey show say 93 percent of academics believe say students dey use generative AI do their assignment, and 63 percent see say students' thinking capacity dey reduce.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, wey be AI wey people fit trust, good behaviour, fairness and policy, dis kind ministers statement wey big like dis give Wits AHEAD one standard wey di whole world recognize for how public accountability for AI governance suppose be, wey universities and government people for Global South fit quote direct.

UNESCO · UN agency ministerial statement

entry.title: University of Alaska regents weigh a system-wide AI policy for every campus
entry.summary:
Di Board of Regents of University of Alaska don look one draft artificial intelligence policy wey go make all im three campuses put AI implementation plan for ground for students, staff and lecturers. Di draft tok say dem must protect human judgement, keep data privacy and security, and use AI to open education services to more people. Dem plan feedback sessions till autumn 2026 and dem wan approve am finally for di November regents meeting.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 6 na about responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy. One public university system wey dey build im AI governance from scratch, for public, while di regents dey ask question about whether dem get di capacity to monitor am, na governance model wey Wits AHEAD suppose dey follow as e dey write im own policy guidance.

Alaska Public Media · Public broadcaster report

entry.title: World Bank opens free AI skills training to young people across 44 African countries
entry.summary:
World Bank don launch 'The Job I Hope For', wey dey invite young people from 18 years and above for 44 kontris for Sub-Saharan Africa to register for free online training on how generative AI dey work, how to write prompt, and AI ethics. Di training go run for English and French for October 2026. Di programme dey answer one continent wey dem expect say more than 600 million young people go enta labour market by 2050, and e dey ask each person to first tok di kind work wey e dey hope for before e begin build di AI skills wey go carry am go dia.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 4 na about AI, wetin graduates fit do, work opportunity and just transition. Free AI skills programme wey cover di whole continent, wey dem aim straight for young people wey dey enta work, na direct test of how dem fit build training for plenty people for di same labour markets wey Wits AHEAD dey study, and e fit be partner or model wey we suppose dey watch.

World Bank · Intergovernmental body brief

entry.title: Systematic review finds AI training for future primary maths teachers is still too brief to stick
entry.summary:
Researchers for three universities for Portugal do systematic review of 11 peer-reviewed studies on how dem dey train primary school teachers wey never start work to use AI for teaching mathematics. Most of di training na short session wey dem just add to courses wey dey already, no be full module, and e cover AI awareness and practical use well but ethics and critical evaluation no dey consistent, so small evidence dey say di skills dey enta real classroom.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 3 na about AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education. Di four important areas wey di review point out, awareness, literacy and prompting, pedagogical integration and critical evaluation, give Wits AHEAD clear checklist to design im own teacher-training work instead of one-time AI workshop.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed systematic review

entry.title: New scale measures students' skill at using AI responsibly in assessed work
entry.summary:
Researchers for three institutions for China don develop and confam one eighteen-item scale wey dey measure how well higher education students understand assessment criteria, how dem dey disclose dia AI use, and how dem dey keep academic integrity when dem dey use generative AI for coursework. Dem test am with 486 students and later with another 798, di scale show reliable five-factor structure and e link well well to how students dey engage wit feedback and dia mind to act wit integrity.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 1 cover generative AI for higher education: teaching, assessment and integrity. One tool wey dem don confam like dis give institutions practical way to measure and build students assessment know-how, instead of just depend on detection software or blanket ban.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Prescriptive AI model flags Ecuadorian students at highest dropout risk, and what would change it
entry.summary:
Researchers for one public university for Ecuador build one prescriptive analytics framework, wey dem track 2,500 students wey enter between 2020 and 2024, wey no just predict dropout risk well well (ROC-AUC 0.95 to 0.97) but e also identify di smallest change wey fit work, like passing extra credit early or better internet for house, wey fit move student comot from di highest-risk group. First-year grades, early credit progress, money wahala, and internet for house na di strongest signs.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 2 cover AI and predictive analytics for student success. Dis one move early-warning analytics from just marking students wey dey risk to prescribing specific, cheap intervention, one model wey Wits AHEAD fit point to for dia own student-success work for places wey get similar resources.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Largest meta-analysis yet finds AI-supported STEM teaching has a real, moderate effect on learning
entry.summary:
One meta-analysis wey combine 35 experimental and quasi-experimental studies find out say AI-supported teaching dey produce moderate positive effect wey get statistical meaning for STEM learning outcomes (g = 0.67). Di gains dey strongest for high school students, and interventions wey last one to two months show say na dem be di most effective duration wey dem test.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 3 cover AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education. Dis na one of di clearest number-based evidence wey dem don get so far say AI-supported STEM teaching dey work well, and di finding about di best length of intervention dey useful direct for how Wits AHEAD dey design and time dia own STEM programmes.

Journal of Intelligence · Peer-reviewed meta-analysis

entry.title: Gates Foundation commits 1 billion US dollars over two years to equitable AI
entry.summary:
Gates Foundation don promise at least 1 billion US dollars for di next two years to build and deliver artificial intelligence wey go fair for everybody, wit 400 million for education, 400 million for health, 100 million for agriculture and 100 million for AI training data for languages wey no dey get enough attention. Di promise come togeda wit di foundation number ten Goalkeepers report, wey dem call Make This Matter: AI, Equity and the Choice We Can't Delay.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Pillar 6 dey ask who dey design AI wit responsibility and for who. Charity money wey big like dis, wey dem target to close di gap for di poorest regions, go decide which AI-for-education tools go reach di Global South classrooms wey Wits AHEAD dey study.

Gates Foundation · Foundation press release accompanying its Goalkeepers report
